title: Conditional Counterfactual Mean Embeddings: Doubly Robust Estimation and Learning Rates
claim: Our doubly robust estimator stays accurate under nuisance misspecification and recovers multimodal distributions, while baseline estimators degrade or bias.
layout: 3 panels: MSE grid (3x3), density grid (2x3), digit mosaic (3x10)
description: A three-panel results figure. Panel (a), on the left, is a 3x3 grid of line plots of MSE against sample size on a log scale. The columns are Ridge Regression, Deep Feature and Neural-Kernel. The rows are Both Correct, wrong propensity model (π̂) and wrong outcome model (μ̂0). Four methods appear in a shared legend at the top: DR in orange, IPW in blue, PI in green and One-Step in pink, each with shaded error bands. Panel (b), top right, is a 2x3 grid of density curves for two profiles, v1 and v2. A black ground-truth curve with two modes is compared against blue DR bands and red One-Step bands, which show median lines with 50% and 90% intervals. The DR curves track the ground truth more closely. Panel (c), bottom right, is a 3x10 grid of white-on-black handwritten MNIST digits 0-9. The rows show the oracle, DR and One-Step estimates.
caption: (a) MSE vs.\ sample size for three methods (columns) under three misspecification scenarios (rows). Shaded regions indicate standard errors over 10 seeds; (b) Estimated counterfactual densities for profiles $v_1$ (top) and $v_2$ (bottom) defined in Appendix [ref] over 30 runs at $n=10000$. Blue: DR; Red: One-Step. Solid lines are medians; dark and light regions show pointwise 50th and 90th percentile intervals; (c) Empirical mode for each class under three density estimates. Row 1: Oracle estimates on clean data. Row 2: DR estimates (proposed). Row 3: One-Step estimates.
abstract: A complete understanding of heterogeneous treatment effects requires fully capturing the conditional distribution of the counterfactual outcomes. To this end, we propose the Conditional Counterfactual Mean Embeddings (CCME), a framework that embeds conditional distributions of counterfactual outcomes into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Under this framework, we develop a two-stage meta-estimator for CCME that accommodates any RKHS-valued regression in each stage. Based on this meta-estimator, we develop three practical CCME estimators: (1) Ridge Regression estimator, (2) Deep Feature estimator that parameterizes the feature map by a neural network, and (3) Neural-Kernel estimator that performs RKHS-valued regression, with the coefficients parameterized by a neural network. We provide finite-sample convergence rates for all estimators, establishing that they possess the double robustness property. Our experiments demonstrate that our estimators accurately recover distributional features including multimodal structure of conditional counterfactual distributions. Our code is available at https://github.com/donlap/Conditional-Counterfactual-Mean-Embeddings.
